blocker.reason: Upstream dependency conflict: rusqlite 0.41 requires libsqlite3-sys ^0.39, but sqlx-sqlite 0.9.0 (latest published) declares libsqlite3-sys >=0.30.1,<0.38.0; both crates declare links="sqlite3" so Cargo cannot resolve the bump. Every version sqlx-sqlite 0.9.0 allows is affected by RUSTSEC-2026-0459.
blocker.needs: An upstream SQLx patch release that relaxes the libsqlite3-sys upper bound (or a switch away from sqlx-sqlite, which is a product decision), OR an owner-recorded risk acceptance for RUSTSEC-2026-0459 (local vector: victim must open attacker-writable files). Until then CP.2 (cargo deny advisories) cannot be green.

notes: Planner delivery persisted verbatim by the orchestrator (the Plan session had no file-write tool).
Wire reality at the base commit: check-wire-contract.mjs reads crates/warshad/src/lib.rs, so STD.9 is a real gate for every lib.rs packet, not decoration.
Arch rule R1 (core is leaf) and R2 (pipeline must not depend on the daemon) are why K4 defines its own allow-list seam in the pipeline instead of importing warshad::auth::ProcessPolicy.
RunStatus gains no variant in K2: the enum is wire-visible to packages/client, which is out of scope; interruption is Paused plus an {action: run_interrupted} event.
